'''Betty Smith Holzendorf''' (April 5, 1939{{spaced ndash}}February 29, 2024) was a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] politician from [[Florida]] who served as a member of the [[Florida House of Representatives]] from the [[Florida's 16th House of Representatives district|16th district]] from 1988 to 1992 and as a member of the [[Florida Senate]] from the [[Florida's 2nd Senate district|2nd district]] from 1992 to 2002.

==Life and career==
Holzendorf was born in Jacksonville on April 5, 1939.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=paFmAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Holzendorf+Betty+Smith%22|title=Who's who in the South and Southwest|date=March 2, 2005|publisher=Marquis Who's Who|isbn=978-0-8379-0835-9 |via=Google Books}}</ref> She graduated from [[Edward Waters College]] and the [[University of North Florida]], both in Jacksonville. She married King Holzendorf who served as a city councilman in Jacksonville.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jacksonville.com/article/20091017/NEWS/801226316?template=ampart|title=Motive a mystery in slaying of father to 7 - News - The Florida Times-Union - Jacksonville, FL|website=www.jacksonville.com|access-date=February 14, 2019|archive-date=February 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215143934/https://www.jacksonville.com/article/20091017/NEWS/801226316?template=ampart|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the 1960s she was an administrative aide to mayor [[Jake Godbold]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uEZZB0rlGrYC&q=betty+holzendorf&pg=PA66|title=Ebony|date=April 14, 1981|publisher=Johnson Publishing Company|via=Google Books}}</ref>

Holzendorf was defeated in 2003 in a race for the [[Mayor of Jacksonville]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news4jax.com/news/those-who-would-be-mayor|title=Those Who Would Be Mayor|date=March 11, 2003|website=WJXT|access-date=February 15, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.duvalelections.org/portals/duval/archive/OfficeCandidate.aspx986.htm|title=Duval County Supervisor of Elections|website=www.duvalelections.org|access-date=February 15, 2019|archive-date=February 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215102753/https://www.duvalelections.org/portals/duval/archive/OfficeCandidate.aspx986.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> The ''[[Jacksonville Daily Record]]'' interviewed her during her mayoral campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jaxdailyrecord.com/article/conversation-betty-holzendorf|title=A conversation with... Betty Holzendorf &#124; Jax Daily Record|date=March 11, 2003|website=Financial News & Daily Record - Jacksonville, Florida}}</ref>

Holzendorf died on February 29, 2024, at the age of 84.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wokv.com/news/local/duval-county/betty-holzendorf-1939-2024-longtime-florida-legislator-who-represented-duval-dies-age-84/DL3DB562FVD7LDBFTJKC75ZZTY/|title=Betty Holzendorf, 1939-2024: Longtime Florida legislator who represented Duval dies at the age of 84|date=February 29, 2024|website=104.5 WOKV}}</ref> Betty Holzendorf Drive In Jacksonville is named in her honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jaxdailyrecord.com/article/skinner-land-proposed-for-office-retail-commercial-residential-and-assisted-living|title=Skinner land proposed for office, retail, commercial, residential and assisted living - Jax Daily Record|date=November 8, 2017|website=Financial News & Daily Record - Jacksonville, Florida|access-date=February 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108170133/https://www.jaxdailyrecord.com/article/skinner-land-proposed-for-office-retail-commercial-residential-and-assisted-living|archive-date=November 8, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>
